overall.summary: The new Paused state can be entered but is not integrated into the public state representation or any path that can leave it.

observations.title: Incomplete paused-state lifecycle
observations.principle: A new domain state must be handled across every boundary and supported transition.
observations.summary: Jobs can enter Paused, but the API reports that state as unknown and resumable never recognizes it.
observations.impact: A successful pause leaves callers with a state the public API cannot represent or recover from.
observations.recommendation: Define the intended paused lifecycle, map Paused explicitly at the API boundary, implement its supported transition, and validate the round trip.
observations.tradeoffs: If resume is intentionally deferred, reject pause in this release or expose the limitation explicitly instead of creating a terminal state accidentally.

evidence.detail: The pause operation transitions a running job into Paused.
The API falls through to unknown for the new state.
The resumable decision is hard-coded false for every state.

observations.title: Missing paused-state boundary validation
observations.principle: Validation should cover the externally observable behavior and the risky state transition, not only the local assignment.
observations.summary: The test proves that pause mutates the enum but does not exercise how the new state is presented or recovered.
observations.impact: The incomplete API integration can pass while the local transition test remains green.
observations.recommendation: Add a scenario that pauses a running job and verifies the public state plus the intended next transition.
observations.tradeoffs: One lifecycle-level scenario is more valuable here than exhaustive unit cases for each match arm.

evidence.detail: The only test ends after checking the internal enum value.

observations.title: Defective nil-guard on configuration spec
observations.principle: Initialization contracts for core config objects must be enforced on all paths before use; a guard that only activates when the field is already nil does not protect callers.
observations.summary: set_version_vulnerable only calls init_config under the condition that spec is already absent, leaving the initialization contract incomplete.
observations.impact: Callers relying on the guard may observe uninitialized or partially initialized specs on some paths.
observations.recommendation: Make init_config unconditional from all public setters (as in set_version_clean) or remove the redundant outer guard so the helper always ensures a non-nil spec.
observations.tradeoffs: If lazy init is intentional, callers must still guarantee the field before any use that assumes it is present.

evidence.detail: The vulnerable setter guards the init call on spec being none.
init_config itself only populates inside the same nil check.

strengths.summary: The transition rejects invalid source states before mutation.
